title: The Songbook of the Old Mill House Revisited
premise: Isandro Blackwood, a vineyard owner drowning in debts inherited with the estate, agrees to a fake date with Marisol Vega — a pastry chef whose bakery lease expires in three weeks — to survive his family's reunion. What begins as mutual convenience turns real by dessert, but their families are entangled in an old lawsuit over the mill house property that could save Isandro's vineyard only by destroying Marisol's bakery. When Isandro discovers his uncle falsified documents to seize the mill house decades ago, he must choose between using the corruption to clear his debts or exposing it and losing everything. He chooses justice outside the law's slow machinery, testifying publicly at the reunion itself; the vineyard is sold, but Marisol's lease is saved, and they open a small wine-and-bakery counter together in the old mill house.
about_author: Oscar Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent years covering property disputes and county fairs before turning to romance. They write love stories set in places where everyone knows everyone's business and justice arrives late, if at all.

chapters.title: A Date of Convenience
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Desperate to avoid his family's pity at the Blackwood reunion, Isandro hires Marisol — who needs a favor from his lawyer cousin for her expiring lease — to pose as his girlfriend. Their banter is sharp, transactional, and oddly easy. The emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing a fellow survivor, each convinced the arrangement costs nothing.

chapters.title: Dessert and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the reunion dinner, Marisol witnesses the family's casual cruelty toward Isandro and improvises a defense that lands too sincerely. Afterwards, they discover her bakery sits on land the Blackwoods claim through the disputed mill house deed. The beat: the fake date curdles into something real just as their interests collide.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Digging into the deed to save the vineyard, Isandro finds his uncle forged their grandmother's signature decades ago — proof that could void the claim and free Marisol's lease, but also destroy the family fortune he's mortgaged his life to. The beat: rising dread as justice and self-preservation split apart, and he tells Marisol the truth.

chapters.title: What the Mill House Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the reunion's final night, Isandro publicly exposes the forgery, forfeiting the inheritance and the vineyard; Marisol, moved, tears up her own escape plan to stand beside him. Weeks later, the mill house opens as their shared wine-and-bakery counter. The beat: both choose the person over the prize, and find it was never really a sacrifice.
